claim: Neuroblastoma is a common pediatric solid tumor that arises from neural crest cells, typically in the adrenal medulla or paraspinal ganglia with metastases to bone and bone marrow in high-risk cases.
source: Neuroblastoma is a common pediatric solid tumor that arises from neural crest cells, typically in the adrenal medulla or paraspinal ganglia with metastases to bone and bone marrow in high-risk cases (Maris, 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Maris, 2010, which provides external scholarly support for this characterization of neuroblastoma.

claim: Neuroblastoma remains a leading cause of childhood cancer-related death despite the use of multimodal dose-intensive chemotherapy, radiation therapy and immunotherapeutic strategies.
source: It remains a leading cause of childhood cancer-related death despite the use of multimodal dose-intensive chemotherapy, radiation therapy and immunotherapeutic strategies (Smith et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Smith et al., 2010, providing external evidence for the mortality and treatment challenges.

claim: Highly penetrant, heritable ALK mutations have been identified as the major cause of familial neuroblastoma.
source: Highly penetrant, heritable ALK mutations have been identified as the major cause of familial neuroblastoma.
evidence: This claim is supported by established scientific knowledge about the genetic basis of familial neuroblastoma.

claim: Somatic mutations in ALK are found as oncogenic drivers in up to 10% of sporadic neuroblastoma with a gene amplification frequency of approximately 2%.
source: Somatic mutations in ALK are also found as oncogenic drivers in up to 10% of sporadic neuroblastoma with a gene amplification frequency of approximately 2% (Chen et al., 2008; George et al., 2008; Janoueix-Lerosey et al., 2008; Mossé et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations (Chen et al., 2008; George et al., 2008; Janoueix-Lerosey et al., 2008; Mossé et al., 2008) providing external evidence for the frequency of ALK mutations and amplifications.

claim: ALK mutations cause single amino acid substitution in the ALK kinase domain and result in autophosphorylation and constitutive activation of the RTK.
source: These mutations cause single amino acid substitution in the ALK kinase domain and result in autophosphorylation and constitutive activation of the RTK.
evidence: This claim is supported by established knowledge about the molecular mechanism of ALK mutations.

claim: The most frequently mutated residues in ALK, R1275, F1174 and F1245, account for 85% of mutations in ALK.
source: The most frequently mutated residues, R1275, F1174 and F1245, account for 85% of mutations in ALK (Bresler et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Bresler et al., 2014, providing external evidence for the distribution of ALK mutations.

claim: Crizotinib is a small-molecule adenosine triphosphate (ATP)-competitive inhibitor that has activity against ALK, MET and ROS1 RTKs.
source: Crizotinib is a small-molecule adenosine triphosphate (ATP)-competitive inhibitor that has activity against ALK, MET and ROS1 RTKs (Cui et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Cui et al., 2011, providing external evidence for crizotinib's mechanism and targets.

claim: Therapy with crizotinib has significant clinical activity in patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), anaplastic large cell lymphoma (ALCL) and inflammatory myofibroblastic tumor (IMT) that harbor ALK rearrangements.
source: Therapy with crizotinib has significant clinical activity in patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), anaplastic large cell lymphoma (ALCL) and inflammatory myofibroblastic tumor (IMT) that harbor ALK rearrangements (Kwak et al., 2010; Mossé et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Kwak et al., 2010 and Mossé et al., 2013, providing external evidence for crizotinib's clinical activity.

claim: Only one of 11 neuroblastoma patients with known ALK mutations responded to crizotinib in an early phase clinical trial.
source: However, only one of 11 neuroblastoma patients with known ALK mutations responded in this study.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Mossé et al., 2013 (referenced in the preceding sentence), providing external evidence for the clinical trial results.

claim: Ceritinib is a second-generation ALK inhibitor that has 20-fold higher potency against ALK than crizotinib in enzymatic assays.
source: Ceritinib is a second-generation ALK inhibitor that has 20-fold higher potency against ALK than crizotinib in enzymatic assays (Marsilje et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Marsilje et al., 2013, providing external evidence for ceritinib's potency.

claim: Ceritinib has demonstrated marked clinical activity in both crizotinib-naive and crizotinib-relapsed ALK-positive NSCLC patients.
source: It has demonstrated marked clinical activity in both crizotinib-naive and crizotinib-relapsed ALK-positive NSCLC patients (Shaw et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Shaw et al., 2014, providing external evidence for ceritinib's clinical activity.

claim: In a phase I study of pediatric cancer, only two of 14 neuroblastoma patients with known ALK mutations showed partial responses to ceritinib.
source: In a phase I study of pediatric cancer, 14 neuroblastoma patients with known ALK mutations were treated with ceritinib (Birgit Geoerger et al., 2015). To date, only two patients showed partial responses, and one patient with ALK F1174L mutated neuroblastoma had shrinkage of a retroperitoneal mass.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Birgit Geoerger et al., 2015, providing external evidence for the clinical trial results.

claim: ALK F1174L and F1174C mutations were identified as acquired resistance mutations in oncogenic ALK fusion proteins during crizotinib and ceritinib treatments, respectively.
source: ALK F1174L and F1174C mutations were identified as acquired resistance mutations in oncogenic ALK fusion proteins during crizotinib and ceritinib treatments, respectively (Friboulet et al., 2014; Sasaki et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Friboulet et al., 2014 and Sasaki et al., 2010, providing external evidence for resistance mutations.

claim: The F1174L mutation increased ATP-binding affinity of ALK and reduced its susceptibility to crizotinib inhibition.
source: Biochemical analyses revealed that the F1174L mutation increased ATP-binding affinity of ALK and reduced its susceptibility to crizotinib inhibition (Bresler et al., 2014, Bresler et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Bresler et al., 2014 and Bresler et al., 2011, providing external evidence for the biochemical mechanism.

claim: PF06463922 exhibits superior antitumor activity in neuroblastoma xenografts harboring the ALK F1174L mutation.
source: In a recent study, Infarinato and colleagues have shown that PF06463922, a highly potent ALK inhibitor for wild-type ALK and various ALK mutants, exhibits superior antitumor activity in neuroblastoma xenografts harboring the ALK F1174L mutation (Infarinato et al., 2016), providing a rationale for assessing the efficacy of newer generation ALK inhibitors in clinical trials for treating patients with ALK-mutated neuroblastoma.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Infarinato et al., 2016, providing external evidence for PF06463922's antitumor activity.

claim: The majority of tumors that harbor the crizotinib- and ceritinib-sensitive ALK R1275Q mutation did not respond in the trials of crizotinib and ceritinib in neuroblastoma patients.
source: However, the majority of the tumors that harbor the crizotinib- and ceritinib-sensitive ALK R1275Q mutation did not respond in the trials of crizotinib and ceritinib in neuroblastoma patients (Mossé et al., 2013; Birgit Geoerger et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Mossé et al., 2013 and Birgit Geoerger et al., 2015, providing external evidence for clinical trial results.

claim: ALK mutations have been identified in both low- and high-risk neuroblastoma with equal frequency.
source: In addition, ALK mutations have been identified in both low- and high-risk neuroblastoma with equal frequency (Bresler et al., 2014), suggesting that activated ALK cooperates with other oncogenic aberrations to define high- versus low-risk tumors.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Bresler et al., 2014, providing external evidence for the distribution of ALK mutations across risk groups.

claim: ALK mutations are frequently observed in MYCN-amplified neuroblastomas, and most of ALK amplifications co-occur with MYCN amplification.
source: For example, ALK mutations are frequently observed in MYCN-amplified neuroblastomas, and most of ALK amplifications co-occur with MYCN amplification (George et al., 2008; Bresler et al., 2014; Bagci et al., 2012; De Brouwer et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to George et al., 2008; Bresler et al., 2014; Bagci et al., 2012; and De Brouwer et al., 2010, providing external evidence for the co-occurrence.

claim: Constitutively activated ALK synergizes with MYCN overexpression in inducing neuroblastoma in animal models.
source: Constitutively, activated ALK synergizes with MYCN overexpression in inducing neuroblastoma in animal models, and the co-occurrence of ALK F1174 mutations and MYCN amplification defines a subset of neuroblastoma patients with particularly poor outcome (Berry et al., 2012; Heukamp et al., 2012; Zhu et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Berry et al., 2012; Heukamp et al., 2012; and Zhu et al., 2012, providing external evidence for the synergistic effect.

claim: The co-occurrence of ALK F1174 mutations and MYCN amplification defines a subset of neuroblastoma patients with particularly poor outcome.
source: Constitutively, activated ALK synergizes with MYCN overexpression in inducing neuroblastoma in animal models, and the co-occurrence of ALK F1174 mutations and MYCN amplification defines a subset of neuroblastoma patients with particularly poor outcome (Berry et al., 2012; Heukamp et al., 2012; Zhu et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Berry et al., 2012; Heukamp et al., 2012; and Zhu et al., 2012, providing external evidence for the clinical outcome.

claim: MDM2 functions as an E3 ubiquitin ligase that targets p53 for proteasome-mediated degradation.
source: MDM2 functions as an E3 ubiquitin ligase that targets p53 for proteasome-mediated degradation.
evidence: This claim is supported by established scientific knowledge about MDM2's molecular function.

claim: p53 protein plays a critical role in tumor suppression by regulating the expression of genes involved in cell cycle arrest and apoptosis.
source: p53 protein plays a critical role in tumor suppression by regulating the expression of genes involved in cell cycle arrest and apoptosis.
evidence: This claim is supported by established scientific knowledge about p53's role in tumor suppression.

claim: CGM097 exerts its antitumor effects by stabilizing p53 and activating p53 pathways.
source: Thus, CGM097 exerts its antitumor effects by stabilizing p53 and activating p53 pathways (Jeay et al., 2015; Weisberg et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Jeay et al., 2015 and Weisberg et al., 2015, providing external evidence for CGM097's mechanism of action.

claim: To elicit antitumor responses, tumor cells must possess wild-type or functional p53 for CGM097 to be effective.
source: However, to elicit these responses, tumor cells must possess wild-type or functional p53 (Jeay et al., 2015; Weisberg et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Jeay et al., 2015 and Weisberg et al., 2015, providing external evidence for the requirement of wild-type p53.

claim: Mutations of TP53 have been reported in less than 2% of neuroblastomas at diagnosis and 15% at relapse.
source: In contrast to the high frequency of TP53 mutations observed in many human cancers of adults, mutations of TP53 have been reported in less than 2% of neuroblastomas at diagnosis and 15% at relapse (Carr-Wilkinson et al., 2010; Tweddle et al., 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Carr-Wilkinson et al., 2010 and Tweddle et al., 2003, providing external evidence for TP53 mutation frequency.

claim: The combination of ceritinib with CGM097 promotes apoptosis in ALK mutant/TP53 wild-type neuroblastoma cell lines.
source: Here, we report that the combination of ceritinib with CGM097 promotes apoptosis in ALK mutant/TP53 wild-type neuroblastoma cell lines and results in complete tumor regression and markedly prolonged survival in neuroblastoma xenograft models.
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in the manuscript, as indicated by the phrase 'we report' and subsequent figures showing experimental results.

claim: The combination of ceritinib with CGM097 results in complete tumor regression and markedly prolonged survival in neuroblastoma xenograft models.
source: Here, we report that the combination of ceritinib with CGM097 promotes apoptosis in ALK mutant/TP53 wild-type neuroblastoma cell lines and results in complete tumor regression and markedly prolonged survival in neuroblastoma xenograft models.
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in the manuscript, specifically in Figure 3A showing tumor volume measurements over time.

claim: Ceritinib and CGM097 combination overcomes acquired ceritinib resistance caused by MYCN upregulation in an ALK-driven neuroblastoma model.
source: In addition, ceritinib and CGM097 combination overcomes acquired ceritinib resistance caused by MYCN upregulation in an ALK-driven neuroblastoma model.
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in the manuscript, specifically in Figures 4 and 5 showing resistance mechanisms and combination effects.

claim: NB-1 cells carry ALK amplification and no ALK mutations in the kinase domain.
source: NB-1 cells, which carry ALK amplification and no ALK mutations in the kinase domain, displayed pronounced dose-dependent decrease in cell viability when treated with the four ALK inhibitors (Figure 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Table 1 showing the genetic characterization of cell lines.

claim: NB-1 cells displayed pronounced dose-dependent decrease in cell viability when treated with ceritinib, crizotinib, alectinib, and PF06463922.
source: NB-1 cells, which carry ALK amplification and no ALK mutations in the kinase domain, displayed pronounced dose-dependent decrease in cell viability when treated with the four ALK inhibitors (Figure 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A, which displays dose-response curves.

claim: The sensitivity of NB-1 to ALK inhibitors matches the potency of these ALK inhibitors in Ba/F3 cells expressing wild-type EML4-ALK as reported by Zou et al. (2015).
source: The sensitivity of NB-1 matches the potency of these ALK inhibitors in Ba/F3 cells expressing wild-type EML4-ALK as reported by Zou et al. (201)5 (Figure 1B) and was reflected by the levels of inhibition of phospho-ALK and the components of the downstream signaling of ALK (Figure 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by comparison of data in Figure 1B with published results from Zou et al., 2015.

claim: The response of NB-1 xenografts to ceritinib was transient, and tumors resumed growth 2 weeks after the start of the treatment.
source: The response of NB-1 xenografts to ceritinib was transient, and tumors resumed growth 2 weeks after the start of the treatment (Figure 3A and Figure 3—source data 1), suggesting that single-agent ALK inhibition may not be sufficient to achieve durable response in a subset of ALK-driven neuroblastoma tumors.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A, which displays tumor volume measurements over time.

claim: All four ALK inhibitors displayed reduced anti-proliferative activity in the neuroblastoma cell lines that harbor the ALK F1174L mutation compared with NB-1.
source: All these four ALK inhibitors displayed reduced anti-proliferative activity in the neuroblastoma cell lines that harbor the ALK F1174L mutation compared with NB-1 (Figure 1A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 1A and 1B comparing dose-response curves and IC50 values.

claim: PF06463922 most robustly inhibited phospho-ALK and phospho-ERK in F1174L-mutated neuroblastoma cell lines.
source: Although PF06463922 most robustly inhibited phospho-ALK and phospho-ERK in these cell lines (Figure 1C), we did not observe significantly greater growth inhibition in the F1174L-mutated cell lines by PF06463922 compared with crizotinib, ceritinib and alectinib (Figure 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C, which displays Western blot analysis of signaling proteins.

claim: PF06463922 did not show significantly greater growth inhibition in the F1174L-mutated cell lines compared with crizotinib, ceritinib and alectinib.
source: Although PF06463922 most robustly inhibited phospho-ALK and phospho-ERK in these cell lines (Figure 1C), we did not observe significantly greater growth inhibition in the F1174L-mutated cell lines by PF06463922 compared with crizotinib, ceritinib and alectinib (Figure 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A comparing dose-response curves.

claim: PF06463922 caused a partial growth inhibition in cell lines with the ALK F1174L mutation.
source: Consistent with prior observations (Infarinato et al., 2016), PF06463922 caused a partial growth inhibition in cell lines with the ALK F1174L mutation (Figure 1A), presumably due to the high specificity of PF06463922 for ALK.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A and is consistent with prior published observations.

claim: The IC50 values for the four ALK inhibitors in the F1174L neuroblastoma cell lines were 10 to 100-fold higher than the IC50 values in Ba/F3 cells expressing EML4-ALK F1174L mutant.
source: In addition, the IC50 values for the four ALK inhibitors in the F1174L neuroblastoma cell lines were 10 to 100-fold higher than the IC50 values in Ba/F3 cells expressing EML4-ALK F1174L mutant (Zou et al., 2015) (Figure 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by comparison of data in Figure 1B with published results from Zou et al., 2015.

claim: Treatment of ceritinib showed limited efficacy in SH-SY5Y xenograft tumors, resulting in slower tumor growth compared with vehicle-treated mice.
source: Treatment of ceritinib showed limited efficacy in SH-SY5Y xenograft tumors, resulting in slower tumor growth compared with vehicle-treated mice (Figure 3A and Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A displaying tumor volume measurements over time.

claim: The TP53 wild-type neuroblastoma cell lines were significantly more sensitive to CGM097 than the TP53 mutant cell lines.
source: Consistent with the mechanism of action of MDM2 inhibitors, the TP53 wild-type neuroblastoma cell lines were significantly more sensitive than the TP53 mutant cell lines.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A and is consistent with the known mechanism of MDM2 inhibitors.

claim: All five TP53 mutant cell lines had IC50 values greater than 11 µM for CGM097.
source: Whereas all five TP53 mutant cell lines had IC50 values greater than 11 µM, the IC50 values of all the TP53 wild-type cell lines were below 3.5 µM (range 0.8–3.5 µM) (Figure 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A displaying IC50 values for different cell lines.

claim: The IC50 values of all the TP53 wild-type cell lines for CGM097 were below 3.5 µM (range 0.8–3.5 µM).
source: Whereas all five TP53 mutant cell lines had IC50 values greater than 11 µM, the IC50 values of all the TP53 wild-type cell lines were below 3.5 µM (range 0.8–3.5 µM) (Figure 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A displaying IC50 values for different cell lines.

claim: CGM097 alone at 50 mg/kg/day demonstrated no inhibition of tumor growth in NB-1, SH-SY5Y, NB-1643, and IMR-32 xenograft models.
source: CGM097 alone at 50 mg/kg/day demonstrated no inhibition of tumor growth in these models (Figure 3A and Figure 3—source data 1), suggesting that single-agent treatment with MDM2 inhibitors is not sufficient to inhibit the growth of TP53 wild-type neuroblastoma tumors expressing wild-type or activated ALK.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A displaying tumor volume measurements over time.

claim: The combinations of ceritinib and CGM097 at concentrations greater than 100 nM resulted in improved growth inhibition compared to treatments with either compound alone in all three TP53 wild-type cell lines.
source: An examination of these matrices indicates that the combinations of ceritinib and CGM097 at the concentrations greater than 100 nM resulted in improved growth inhibition compared to treatments with either compound alone in all three TP53 wild-type cell lines (Figure 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B displaying dose matrices for combination treatments.

claim: The effects of combining ceritinib and CGM097 were synergistic in the three TP53 wild-type cell lines (NB-1, SH-SY5Y, KP-N-RT-BM-1).
source: Isobologram analysis revealed that the effects of combining ceritinib and CGM097 were synergistic in these three cell lines (Figure 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C displaying isobologram analysis.

claim: CGM097 alone was completely ineffective in inhibiting the growth of the TP53-mutated KELLY cells.
source: In contrast to the TP53 wild-type cell lines, CGM097 alone was completely ineffective in inhibiting the growth of the TP53-mutated KELLY cells, and no improved growth inhibition of the combination was observed in these cells (Figure 2B and C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 2B and 2C.

claim: No improved growth inhibition of the ceritinib and CGM097 combination was observed in TP53-mutated KELLY cells.
source: In contrast to the TP53 wild-type cell lines, CGM097 alone was completely ineffective in inhibiting the growth of the TP53-mutated KELLY cells, and no improved growth inhibition of the combination was observed in these cells (Figure 2B and C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 2B and 2C.

claim: CGM097 caused an accumulation in p53 protein itself and the induction of p53 direct effectors, p21 and MDM2 proteins.
source: Effective target inhibition was achieved with CGM097, as evident by an accumulation in p53 protein itself and the induction of p53 direct effectors, p21 and MDM2 proteins (Figure 2D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D displaying Western blot analysis.

claim: Ceritinib caused a reduction of phospho-ALK, phospho-AKT and phospho-ERK signaling.
source: Ceritinib caused a reduction of phospho-ALK, phospho-AKT and phospho-ERK signaling, likewise demonstrating effective target and pathway inhibition (Figure 2D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D displaying Western blot analysis.

claim: CGM097 was unable to induce p53 protein or its downstream effectors in TP53 mutant KELLY cells.
source: As expected, CGM097 was unable to induce p53 protein or its downstream effectors in TP53 mutant KELLY cells as expected (Figure 2D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D displaying Western blot analysis.

claim: CGM097 caused induction of p21 and PUMA, while ceritinib caused induction of p27 and Bim.
source: When the components in the cell cycle and apoptosis pathways were examined, CGM097 caused induction of p21 and PUMA, while ceritinib caused induction of p27 and Bim (Figure 2D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D displaying Western blot analysis.

claim: Ceritinib and CGM097 together induced a complementary, yet non-overlapping set of anti-proliferative and apoptosis-stimulating molecules.
source: Therefore, together ceritinib and CGM097 induced a complementary, yet non-overlapping set of anti-proliferative and apoptosis-stimulating molecules, which resulted in synergistic antitumor effects (Figure 2D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D and is inferred from the observed protein expression patterns.

claim: Only when combined, ceritinib and CGM097 could cause significant increase of cleaved PARP.
source: Only when combined, the two compounds could cause significant increase of cleaved PARP (Figure 2D), suggesting that the combination leads to cell death.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D displaying Western blot analysis of cleaved PARP.

claim: The combination of ceritinib and CGM097 led to complete and durable tumor regressions throughout treatment period in NB-1, SH-SY5Y and NB-1643 models.
source: In contrast to the limited or transient responses to the single-agent treatments, the combination led to complete and durable tumor regressions throughout treatment period in NB-1, SH-SY5Y and NB-1643 models (Figure 3A and Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A displaying tumor volume measurements over time.

claim: Two out of five NB-1 animals showed tumor regrowth two weeks after the combination treatment was stopped.
source: Two (NB-1) or eight (SH-SY5Y) weeks after the combination treatment was stopped, two out of five animals and three out of four animals showed tumor regrowth for NB-1 and SH-SY5Y, respectively (Figure 3A and Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A displaying tumor volume measurements after treatment cessation.

claim: Three out of four SH-SY5Y animals showed tumor regrowth eight weeks after the combination treatment was stopped.
source: Two (NB-1) or eight (SH-SY5Y) weeks after the combination treatment was stopped, two out of five animals and three out of four animals showed tumor regrowth for NB-1 and SH-SY5Y, respectively (Figure 3A and Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A displaying tumor volume measurements after treatment cessation.

claim: The recurrent tumors remained sensitive to the combination treatment of ceritinib and CGM097.
source: The recurrent tumors remained sensitive to the combination treatment (data not shown), suggesting that the residual disease was not completely eliminated in a subset of animals.
evidence: This claim is supported by data that is referenced but not shown in the manuscript.

claim: Neither single agent nor combination treatments showed antitumor activity in the IMR-32 xenograft tumors that contain wild-type ALK and TP53.
source: Neither single agent nor combination treatments showed antitumor activity in the IMR-32 xenograft tumors that contain wild-type ALK and TP53 (Figure 3A and Figure 3—source data 1), suggesting that the combined inhibition of ALK and MDM2 provides an effective treatment in TP53 wild-type neuroblastoma with ALK aberrations.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A displaying tumor volume measurements over time.

claim: The in vivo administration of ceritinib in combination with CGM097 for 3 days resulted in inhibition of phospho-ALK, induction of p21 and increased levels of cleaved PARP compared with either single agent alone.
source: The in vivo administration of ceritinib in combination with CGM097 for 3 days resulted in inhibition of phospho-ALK, induction of p21 and increased levels of cleaved PARP compared with either single agent alone (Figure 3B), which is in agreement with the observations made in vitro.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B displaying Western blot analysis of xenograft tissues.

claim: A marked increase in the expression of a group of genes was found in the ceritinib-resistant NB-1 tumors compared to vehicle-treated tumors.
source: We found a marked increase in the expression of a group of genes in the ceritinib-resistant tumors when we plotted the gene expression levels of the ceritinib-resistant tumors versus those of the vehicle-treated tumors (Figure 4A and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-Seq data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The majority of genes upregulated in the ceritinib-resistant NB-1 tumors encode RPS and RPL proteins of the small and large ribosomal subunits and translation elongation factors.
source: Interestingly, the majority of these genes upregulated in the ceritinib-resistant tumors encode RPS and RPL proteins of the small and large ribosomal subunits and translation elongation factors (Figure 4A).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-Seq data shown in Figure 4A with gene labels.

claim: The Myc family of transcription factors stimulates ribosome biogenesis by enhancing the transcription of ribosomal RNA and genes encoding many RPS and RPL proteins.
source: The Myc family of transcription factors stimulates ribosome biogenesis by enhancing the transcription of ribosomal RNA and genes encoding many RPS and RPL proteins (van Riggelen et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to van Riggelen et al., 2010, providing external evidence for Myc's role in ribosome biogenesis.

claim: MYCN upregulates the transcription of RPS and RPL genes and translation initiation and elongation factors in human neuroblastoma cell lines.
source: In addition, MYCN has been shown to upregulate the transcription of RPS and RPL genes and translation initiation and elongation factors in human neuroblastoma cell lines (Boon et al., 2001).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Boon et al., 2001, providing external evidence for MYCN's transcriptional effects.

claim: Western blot analysis revealed an increase in the expression of MYCN in the NB-1 ceritinib-resistant tumors.
source: Western blot analysis of three individual tumors collected from the vehicle-treated or ceritinib-resistant mice revealed an increase in the expression of MYCN in the NB-1 ceritinib-resistant tumors (Figure 4B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B displaying Western blot analysis.

claim: NB-1R cells showed significantly decreased sensitivity to ceritinib as compared to the parental cell line.
source: The resultant cell line, NB-1R, showed significantly decreased sensitivity to ceritinib as compared to the parental cell line (Figure 5A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A displaying dose-response curves.

claim: Western blot analysis of ceritinib-resistant NB-1R cells revealed markedly increased expression of MYCN.
source: Similar to the observations made in the ceritinib-resistant NB-1 xenografts, Western blot analysis of these ceritinib-resistant cells revealed markedly increased expression of MYCN (Figure 5B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B displaying Western blot analysis.

claim: ALK signaling was strongly suppressed in the NB-1R resistant cells, as exemplified by reduced levels of phospho-ALK, phospho-AKT and phospho-ERK.
source: However, ALK signaling was strongly suppressed in the resistant cells, as exemplified by reduced levels of phospho-ALK, phospho-AKT and phospho-ERK (Figure 5B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B displaying Western blot analysis.

claim: The levels of MYCN were markedly increased in PF06463922-resistant SH-SY5Y and KP-N-RT-BM-1 cell lines compared to their parental cells.
source: The levels of MYCN were again markedly increased in these two PF06463922-resistant cell lines compared to their parental cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B displaying Western blot analysis.

claim: Downregulation of MYCN restored the sensitivity of the NB-1R cells to ceritinib.
source: While MYCN knockdown in DMSO-treated NB-1R cells did not significantly affect the cell viability, downregulation of MYCN restored the sensitivity of the NB-1R cells to ceritinib (Figure 5D), suggesting that both ALK inhibition and reduction in MYCN level are required for inhibiting the growth of NB-1R cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5D displaying cell viability assays with shRNA-mediated MYCN knockdown.

claim: shRNA-mediated downregulation of MYCN resulted in increased levels of phospho-ALK but had no effect on the expression of p53 and p21.
source: In addition, shRNA-mediated downregulation of MYCN resulted in increased levels of phospho-ALK but had no effect on the expression of p53 and p21 (Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2 displaying Western blot analysis.

claim: Expression of p21 was strongly decreased in the ceritinib-resistant NB-1R cells.
source: However, expression of p21, one of the major p53 transcriptional target genes, was strongly decreased in the ceritinib-resistant cells (Figure 5E), indicating that the p53 signaling might be impaired in the NB-1R cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5E displaying Western blot analysis.

claim: CGM097 treatment resulted in an increase in p53 expression and induction of its target genes, including p21, MDM2 and PUMA in NB-1R cells.
source: CGM097 treatment resulted in an increase in p53 expression and induction of its target genes, including p21, MDM2 and PUMA (Figure 5F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5F displaying Western blot analysis.

claim: CGM097 restored the sensitivity of the NB-1R, SH-SY5YR and KP-N-RT-BM-1R cells to ceritinib or PF06463922 to a level comparable to that in the parental cells.
source: In addition, CGM097 restored the sensitivity of the NB-1R, SH-SY5YR and KP-N-RT-BM-1R cells to ceritinib or PF06463922 to a level comparable to that in the parental cells (Figure 5G and Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5G and Figure 5—figure supplement 1C displaying cell viability assays.

claim: Ceritinib in combination with CGM097 caused increased anti-proliferative activity and decreased viability of NB-1R cells compared to either agent alone.
source: Ceritinib in combination with CGM097 caused increased anti-proliferative activity and decreased viability of NB-1R cells compared to either agent alone (Figure 5G), presumably through induction of stronger apoptosis, evident by induction of cleaved PARP (Figure 5F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 5F and 5G.

claim: Under CGM097 monotherapy treatment, ceritinib-resistant NB-1 tumors continued to grow in vivo.
source: Under CGM097 monotherapy treatment, tumors continued to grow (Figure 5H).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5H displaying tumor volume measurements over time.

claim: The combination of ceritinib and CGM097 led to fast tumor regressions in ceritinib-resistant NB-1 tumors in vivo.
source: In contrast, the combination treatment led to fast tumor regressions (red curve in Figure 5H).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5H displaying tumor volume measurements over time.

claim: CGM097 alone could not reverse the outgrowth of ceritinib-resistant NB-1 tumors.
source: CGM097 alone could not reverse the outgrowth of ceritinib-resistant tumors (dark blue curve in Figure 5H), indicating that both ALK inhibition and p53 activation are required for inhibiting the growth of ceritinib-resistant tumors.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5H displaying tumor volume measurements over time.

claim: The occurrence of resistance was prevented when the tumors were treated with ceritinib in combination with CGM097 from the start.
source: The occurrence of resistance was prevented all together when the tumors were treated with ceritinib in combination with CGM097 from the start (grey curve in Figure 5H), similar to the results shown in Figure 3A.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5H displaying tumor volume measurements over time.

claim: Patients with ALK-mutated neuroblastoma responded less favorably to crizotinib and ceritinib than pediatric patients with ALK-rearranged tumors, such as ALCL and IMT.
source: Although the identification of activating ALK mutations and the demonstration of the oncogenic role of mutant ALK have established ALK as a therapeutic target in neuroblastoma, clinical studies of crizotinib and ceritinib in pediatric cancers have shown that patients with ALK-mutated neuroblastoma responded less favorably than pediatric patients with ALK-rearranged tumors, such as ALCL and IMT (Mossé et al., 2013; Birgit Geoerger et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Mossé et al., 2013 and Birgit Geoerger et al., 2015, providing external evidence for clinical trial results.

claim: Crizotinib inhibited growth of neuroblastoma xenografts expressing ALK R1275Q or amplified wild-type ALK, but failed to inhibit growth of xenografts harboring F1174L-mutated ALK.
source: Previous preclinical work has shown that crizotinib inhibited growth of neuroblastoma xenografts expressing ALK R1275Q or amplified wild-type ALK, but failed to inhibit growth of xenografts harboring F1174L-mutated ALK (Bresler et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Bresler et al., 2011, providing external evidence for crizotinib's activity in xenograft models.

claim: ALK inhibition synergizes with chemotherapy or CDK4 inhibition in preclinical models of neuroblastoma.
source: Previous studies have shown that ALK inhibition synergizes with chemotherapy or CDK4 inhibition in preclinical models of neuroblastoma (Krytska et al., 2016; Wood et al., 2016), and a clinical trial (NCT02780128) for testing the combination of ceritinib and ribociclib in ALK-mutant neuroblastoma patients is ongoing.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Krytska et al., 2016 and Wood et al., 2016, providing external evidence for combination strategies.

claim: Targeted disruption of the MDM2/p53 interaction by small molecule MDM2 antagonists suppresses the proliferation of both chemoresistant and sensitive neuroblastoma cell lines with wild-type TP53.
source: In agreement with our own work using CGM097 (Figure 2A), targeted disruption of the MDM2/p53 interaction by the small molecule MDM2 antagonists, such as nutlin-3 and RG7388, suppresses the proliferation of both chemoresistant and sensitive neuroblastoma cell lines with wild-type TP53 (Chen et al., 2015; Van Maerken et al., 2009, 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Chen et al., 2015; Van Maerken et al., 2009, 2006, and is consistent with the authors' own data.

claim: MYCN-amplified and TP53 wild-type neuroblastoma cell lines show remarkable sensitivities to MDM2 antagonists in vitro.
source: MYCN-amplified and TP53 wild-type neuroblastoma cell lines show remarkable sensitivities to MDM2 antagonists in vitro (Chen et al., 2015; Van Maerken et al., 2006; Gamble et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Chen et al., 2015; Van Maerken et al., 2006; and Gamble et al., 2012, providing external evidence for MDM2 antagonist sensitivity.

claim: MDM2 contributes to tumorigenesis in a MYCN-driven transgenic mouse model for neuroblastoma, and its haploinsufficiency reduces MYCN-driven tumor incidence and inhibits tumor growth via p53-mediated apoptosis.
source: In addition, MDM2 contributes to tumorigenesis in a MYCN-driven transgenic mouse model for neuroblastoma, and its haploinsufficency reduces MYCN-driven tumor incidence and inhibits tumor growth via p53-mediated apoptosis (Chen et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Chen et al., 2009, providing external evidence for MDM2's role in MYCN-driven neuroblastoma.

claim: This is the first work that shows upregulation of MYCN acts as a mechanism by which ALK-driven neuroblastoma cells develop resistance to ALK inhibitors.
source: To our knowledge, this is the first work that shows upregulation of MYCN acts as a mechanism by which ALK-driven neuroblastoma cells develop resistance to ALK inhibitors.
evidence: This claim is supported by the authors' own experimental data presented in Figures 4 and 5, representing a novel finding.

claim: ALK- and MYCN-amplified NB-1 cells rapidly develop resistance to ceritinib even though they are extremely sensitive to ceritinib in culture with an IC50 value less than 50 nM.
source: We found that ALK- and MYCN-amplified NB-1 cells rapidly develop resistance to ceritinib even though they are extremely sensitive to ceritinib in culture with an IC50 value less than 50 nM.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 1 and 5 demonstrating the IC50 value and resistance development.

claim: ALK F1174L occurs at a higher frequency in MYCN-amplified tumors.
source: Given the observations that ALK F1174L occurs at a higher frequency in MYCN-amplified tumors and almost all ALK-amplified tumors are also MYCN-amplified, it is unlikely that durable responses can be achieved by targeting ALK alone.
evidence: This claim is supported by established knowledge from the literature about the co-occurrence of ALK and MYCN alterations.

claim: Almost all ALK-amplified tumors are also MYCN-amplified.
source: Given the observations that ALK F1174L occurs at a higher frequency in MYCN-amplified tumors and almost all ALK-amplified tumors are also MYCN-amplified, it is unlikely that durable responses can be achieved by targeting ALK alone.
evidence: This claim is supported by established knowledge from the literature about the co-occurrence of ALK and MYCN alterations.

claim: Tumor growth was observed 2 to 8 weeks after discontinuation of ceritinib and CGM097 combination treatment in neuroblastoma xenografts.
source: Although ceritinib in combination with CGM097 induced complete and sustained tumor regression for the duration of the treatment in xenograft mouse models of neuroblastoma, tumor growth was observed 2 to 8 weeks after discontinuation of the treatment (Figure 3A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A displaying tumor volume measurements after treatment cessation.

claim: Combined inhibition of ALK and MDM2 induced a complementary set of anti-proliferative and pro-apoptotic proteins.
source: Herein, we report that combined inhibition of ALK and MDM2 induced a complementary set of anti-proliferative and pro-apoptotic proteins.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D displaying Western blot analysis of various proteins.

claim: Combination treatment of ceritinib and CGM097 synergistically inhibited proliferation of TP53 wild-type neuroblastoma cells harboring ALK amplification or mutations in vitro.
source: Consequently, this combination treatment synergistically inhibited proliferation of TP53 wild-type neuroblastoma cells harboring ALK amplification or mutations in vitro, and resulted in complete and durable responses in neuroblastoma xenografts derived from these cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 2B and 2C displaying dose matrices and isobologram analysis.

claim: Combination treatment of ceritinib and CGM097 resulted in complete and durable responses in neuroblastoma xenografts derived from TP53 wild-type cells harboring ALK amplification or mutations.
source: Consequently, this combination treatment synergistically inhibited proliferation of TP53 wild-type neuroblastoma cells harboring ALK amplification or mutations in vitro, and resulted in complete and durable responses in neuroblastoma xenografts derived from these cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A displaying tumor volume measurements over time.

claim: Concurrent inhibition of MDM2 and ALK was able to overcome ceritinib resistance conferred by MYCN upregulation in vitro and in vivo.
source: We further demonstrate that concurrent inhibition of MDM2 and ALK was able to overcome ceritinib resistance conferred by MYCN upregulation in vitro and in vivo.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 5G and 5H displaying cell viability assays and tumor volume measurements.

claim: The IC50 values of crizotinib, ceritinib, alectinib and PF06463922 on cell proliferation of Ba/F3 cells expressing wild-type EML4-ALK were 88 nM, 25 nM, 39 nM and 2.7 nM, respectively.
source: They reported that the IC50 values of crizotinib, ceritinib, alectinib and PF06463922 on cell proliferation of Ba/F3 cells expressing wild-type EML4-ALK were 88 nM, 25 nM, 39 nM and 2.7 nM, respectively; and 106 nM, 40 nM, 28 nM and 4.8 nM, respectively, in Ba/F3 cells expressing EML4-ALK F1174L mutant.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Zou et al., 2015, providing external evidence for IC50 values in Ba/F3 cells.

claim: The IC50 values of crizotinib, ceritinib, alectinib and PF06463922 on cell proliferation of Ba/F3 cells expressing EML4-ALK F1174L mutant were 106 nM, 40 nM, 28 nM and 4.8 nM, respectively.
source: They reported that the IC50 values of crizotinib, ceritinib, alectinib and PF06463922 on cell proliferation of Ba/F3 cells expressing wild-type EML4-ALK were 88 nM, 25 nM, 39 nM and 2.7 nM, respectively; and 106 nM, 40 nM, 28 nM and 4.8 nM, respectively, in Ba/F3 cells expressing EML4-ALK F1174L mutant.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Zou et al., 2015, providing external evidence for IC50 values in Ba/F3 cells.

evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Table 1 showing the genetic characterization of cell lines.

evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Table 1 showing the genetic characterization of cell lines.

claim: Both ALK inhibition and reduction in MYCN level are required for inhibiting the growth of NB-1R cells.
source: While MYCN knockdown in DMSO-treated NB-1R cells did not significantly affect the cell viability, downregulation of MYCN restored the sensitivity of the NB-1R cells to ceritinib (Figure 5D), suggesting that both ALK inhibition and reduction in MYCN level are required for inhibiting the growth of NB-1R cells.
evidence: This claim is inferred from experimental data shown in Figure 5D, where MYCN knockdown alone did not affect viability but restored ceritinib sensitivity.

claim: Both ALK inhibition and p53 activation are required for inhibiting the growth of ceritinib-resistant tumors.
source: CGM097 alone could not reverse the outgrowth of ceritinib-resistant tumors (dark blue curve in Figure 5H), indicating that both ALK inhibition and p53 activation are required for inhibiting the growth of ceritinib-resistant tumors.
evidence: This claim is inferred from experimental data shown in Figure 5H, where CGM097 alone was ineffective but the combination was effective.

claim: MYCN upregulation may be sufficient to drive proliferation in the presence of ALK inhibitors despite ALK inhibitor-mediated suppression of ALK signaling.
source: These results suggest that despite the ALK inhibitor-mediated suppression of ALK signaling, MYCN upregulation may be sufficient to drive proliferation in the presence of ALK inhibitors.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that resistant cells have suppressed ALK signaling but elevated MYCN and continue to proliferate.

claim: The p53 signaling might be impaired in the NB-1R cells.
source: However, expression of p21, one of the major p53 transcriptional target genes, was strongly decreased in the ceritinib-resistant cells (Figure 5E), indicating that the p53 signaling might be impaired in the NB-1R cells.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation of decreased p21 expression, which is a p53 target gene.

claim: The combination of ceritinib and CGM097 leads to cell death.
source: Only when combined, the two compounds could cause significant increase of cleaved PARP (Figure 2D), suggesting that the combination leads to cell death.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation of increased cleaved PARP, which is a marker of apoptosis.

claim: The residual disease was not completely eliminated in a subset of animals treated with ceritinib and CGM097 combination.
source: The recurrent tumors remained sensitive to the combination treatment (data not shown), suggesting that the residual disease was not completely eliminated in a subset of animals.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that tumors regrew after treatment cessation but remained sensitive to re-treatment.

claim: The combined inhibition of ALK and MDM2 provides an effective treatment in TP53 wild-type neuroblastoma with ALK aberrations.
source: Neither single agent nor combination treatments showed antitumor activity in the IMR-32 xenograft tumors that contain wild-type ALK and TP53 (Figure 3A and Figure 3—source data 1), suggesting that the combined inhibition of ALK and MDM2 provides an effective treatment in TP53 wild-type neuroblastoma with ALK aberrations.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that the combination was effective in ALK-aberrant models but not in wild-type ALK models.

claim: Single-agent ALK inhibition may not be sufficient to achieve durable response in a subset of ALK-driven neuroblastoma tumors.
source: The response of NB-1 xenografts to ceritinib was transient, and tumors resumed growth 2 weeks after the start of the treatment (Figure 3A and Figure 3—source data 1), suggesting that single-agent ALK inhibition may not be sufficient to achieve durable response in a subset of ALK-driven neuroblastoma tumors.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation of transient response to ceritinib monotherapy.

claim: Other pathways may contribute to the survival of the F1174L-mutated neuroblastoma cells in addition to ALK signaling.
source: In addition, the IC50 values for the four ALK inhibitors in the F1174L neuroblastoma cell lines were 10 to 100-fold higher than the IC50 values in Ba/F3 cells expressing EML4-ALK F1174L mutant (Zou et al., 2015) (Figure 1B). These data suggest that, in addition to ALK signaling, other pathways may contribute to the survival of the F1174L-mutated neuroblastoma cells.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that F1174L neuroblastoma cells are less sensitive to ALK inhibitors than Ba/F3 cells with the same mutation.

claim: A combination therapy that consists of an ALK inhibitor and a second agent is required for neuroblastoma tumors that contain ALK aberrations.
source: Altogether, these data suggest that ALK inhibition alone is not sufficient to achieve durable and deep responses in neuroblastoma tumors that contain ALK aberrations, and that a combination therapy that consists of an ALK inhibitor and a second agent is required.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the collective observations of limited efficacy of single-agent ALK inhibitors.

claim: Single-agent treatment with MDM2 inhibitors is not sufficient to inhibit the growth of TP53 wild-type neuroblastoma tumors expressing wild-type or activated ALK.
source: CGM097 alone at 50 mg/kg/day demonstrated no inhibition of tumor growth in these models (Figure 3A and Figure 3—source data 1), suggesting that single-agent treatment with MDM2 inhibitors is not sufficient to inhibit the growth of TP53 wild-type neuroblastoma tumors expressing wild-type or activated ALK.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that CGM097 monotherapy showed no antitumor activity.

claim: The low response rates in clinical studies of crizotinib and ceritinib in neuroblastoma is not likely to be solely attributed to the inherent primary resistance caused by the ALK F1174 substitutions.
source: However, the majority of the tumors that harbor the crizotinib- and ceritinib-sensitive ALK R1275Q mutation did not respond in the trials of crizotinib and ceritinib in neuroblastoma patients (Mossé et al., 2013; Birgit Geoerger et al., 2015). These results suggest that the low response rates in these clinical studies is not likely to be solely attributed to the inherent primary resistance caused by the ALK F1174 substitutions in neuroblastoma.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that even R1275Q-mutant tumors, which are sensitive to these drugs, did not respond well in clinical trials.

claim: Activated ALK cooperates with other oncogenic aberrations to define high- versus low-risk tumors.
source: In addition, ALK mutations have been identified in both low- and high-risk neuroblastoma with equal frequency (Bresler et al., 2014), suggesting that activated ALK cooperates with other oncogenic aberrations to define high- versus low-risk tumors.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that ALK mutations occur equally in low- and high-risk tumors, suggesting other factors determine risk.

claim: The co-occurrence of mutations in ALK with dysregulation in other oncogenic drivers, such as MYCN amplification, may further limit the activity of single-agent ALK inhibitors.
source: Therefore, the co-occurrence of mutations in ALK with dysregulation in other oncogenic drivers, such as MYCN amplification, may further limit the activity of single-agent ALK inhibitors.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observations about co-occurrence of ALK and MYCN alterations and their synergistic effects.

claim: Ceritinib in combination with CGM097 caused increased anti-proliferative activity and decreased viability of NB-1R cells presumably through induction of stronger apoptosis.
source: Ceritinib in combination with CGM097 caused increased anti-proliferative activity and decreased viability of NB-1R cells compared to either agent alone (Figure 5G), presumably through induction of stronger apoptosis, evident by induction of cleaved PARP (Figure 5F).
evidence: This claim involves speculation about the mechanism (apoptosis) based on the observation of cleaved PARP.

claim: PF06463922 caused a partial growth inhibition in cell lines with the ALK F1174L mutation presumably due to the high specificity of PF06463922 for ALK.
source: Consistent with prior observations (Infarinato et al., 2016), PF06463922 caused a partial growth inhibition in cell lines with the ALK F1174L mutation (Figure 1A), presumably due to the high specificity of PF06463922 for ALK.
evidence: This claim involves speculation about the reason for partial inhibition based on the drug's specificity.

claim: Mutationally activated ALK may suppress the apoptotic response induced by MYCN.
source: Mutationally activated ALK may suppress the apoptotic response induced by MYCN, and prolonged treatment with ALK inhibitors can shift the equilibrium between pro-survival and pro-apoptotic pathways, which enables a subset of tumors cells to survive.
evidence: This claim involves speculation about the mechanism by which ALK and MYCN interact.

claim: Prolonged treatment with ALK inhibitors can shift the equilibrium between pro-survival and pro-apoptotic pathways, which enables a subset of tumor cells to survive.
source: Mutationally activated ALK may suppress the apoptotic response induced by MYCN, and prolonged treatment with ALK inhibitors can shift the equilibrium between pro-survival and pro-apoptotic pathways, which enables a subset of tumors cells to survive.
evidence: This claim involves speculation about the mechanism of resistance development.
